title: Model Moat Heatmap: buyer-signal harmonization & vendor threat probes
creator: Caroline Nguyen
description:
Brief summary: Build a concise, repeatable artifact (Model Moat Heatmap) that correlates buyer signals, procurement triggers, and vendor-level threat vectors (availability, latency, quantization compatibility) to help GTM and sales prioritize fallback and procurement playbooks.
Goals: 1) Surface top 12 vendor-model combinations by enterprise-sensitivity; 2) Identify 3 leading threat scenarios (supply outage, quantization incompatibility, regional latency spike) and recommended mitigations; 3) Deliver a dashboard prototype and a 2-page one-pager for sales.
Scope: Quant-based scoring from telemetry (latency, error rate), procurement signals (SLAs, pricing), and qualitative field research (sales interviews). Exclude edge devices and tiny models (under 2B params) for now.
Success metrics: Completed heatmap + scoring notebook; validation with 4 enterprise customers; PRD approved by 03/25.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Heatmap artifact published in Confluence with scoring methodology and data sources listed; 2) Dashboard prototype (Looker/Metabase) connected to sample telemetry; 3) Two validated mitigation playbooks (fallback routing + quantization recommendation) with cost delta estimates; 4) Presentation delivered to Sales & Solutions by due date.
comments: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff: aligned with Sales Ops and Research. Assigned Ravi as PM lead. Action: Research to pull telemetry slices for last 90 days (latency per region, 95th pct).

2026-02-28 — Data pull complete: infra team shared latency buckets and outage events. Noted heavy tail in APAC regions during 02/10–02/12 incident. Linked sample: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/model-telemetry/latency_apac_q1.csv
2026-03-03 — First scoring draft reviewed with Research. Trade-off: weighting latency vs procurement cost debated; decided to expose weighting knobs in notebook rather than hardcode.

2026-03-08 — Design reviewed heatmap mock. Feedback: add an 'operational friction' axis capturing quantization and dependency on proprietary kernels. Design ticket linked: DES-2334-heatmap-legend-proposal
2026-03-11 — Sales validation session scheduled with two enterprise accounts (FinServCo, HealthAI). Captured buyer heuristics: latency sensitivity trumps cost for financial realtime use-cases.
2026-03-14 — Prototype dashboard wired to synthetic dataset; uncovered mismatch in model naming conventions across telemetry and procurement feeds (normalization task created as ENG-9912).
next_steps: 1) ENG to complete normalization (ENG-9912) — blocker for automated scoring. 2) Research to run sensitivity analysis on weighting knobs and publish notebook by 03/20. 3) Schedule demo with Sales on 03/22. 4) Draft procurement playbook and pricing delta table.
risks: - Inconsistent naming across data sources may delay automated scoring. - Vendor contract confidentiality may limit exposure of true pricing; will use anonymized buckets. - Prototype may bias towards telemetry-rich regions (NA/EU).
